react_result.final_narrative_text: Three orthogonal enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP ORA across SMPDB, KEGG and WikiPathways ranks 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00140) as the top hit with an FDR of 4.97×10⁻¹⁸ and a fold-enrichment of 1501, implicating six of the eight input metabolites (estradiol, estrone, androstenedione, DHEA, dihydrotestosterone, testosterone). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00140 as the sole significant hit (p = 5.77×10⁻⁷), with the identical six steroids in its metabolites_hit list. Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring places 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' at rank 1 (p = 1.68×10⁻⁴) with a 14-compound empirical overlap that encompasses every input steroid, reflecting the dense connectivity of this hub in the metabolic network. The tyrosine metabolism branch (mummichog rank 2, p = 0.029) captures 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, the aldehyde product of dopamine deamination by MAO, indicating co-perturbation of the catecholamine arm of tyrosine catabolism. Warfarin is the only metabolite unassigned by all three methods — its coumarin scaffold is structurally unrelated to the steroid nucleus and maps to xenobiotic vitamin K metabolism rather than the sex-steroid axis. The six-driver steroid set forms a coherent biosynthetic chain: DHEA and androstenedione sit upstream at the androgen/estrogen branch point; testosterone and dihydrotestosterone occupy the androgen limb; estradiol and estrone occupy the estrogen limb. Coordinated differential abundance across this entire axis strongly implicates altered steroidogenic enzyme activity — most plausibly CYP17A1, CYP19A1 (aromatase), or HSD17B isoforms — as the mechanistic driver of the treatment effect.
